title: 32-bit value with the wrong word order
summary: A REAL or 32-bit integer spans two registers; the order of the two words is device specific.

sections.heading: Recognize it
sections.body: Communication is error free and the raw words look plausible, but the decoded 32-bit value is absurd.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: Compare the configured word order with the device documentation; if the documentation is unclear, decode the raw words both ways and compare with a known value.

modeled: Deterministic Modbus TCP client and servers: IPv4 subnet rules, address resolution, unit ID handling of gateways, function 03/04 reads, exceptions 01/02/0B, processing time against the configured timeout, INT and REAL values with word order
approximated: One request at a time per connection
omitted: Writes, other function codes and serial bus timing behind gateways
Byte order inside a register (words are big-endian as the protocol defines)

diagnosticMethod: Decode the raw words both ways
troubleshooting.explanation: Swapping the halves of a 32-bit number changes it completely.
